name: Projected cropland under the Towards Sustainability scenario
descriptionShort: Projected area of land used to grow crops, under FAO's "Towards Sustainability" scenario, where food and agriculture systems shift towards more sustainable practices.
descriptionProcessing:
- Values correspond to the world totals published in Table 4.12 of the report, converted from million hectares to hectares.
- The projections start from a 2012 base year (1,567 million hectares, shared by the three scenarios), which is not shown in charts, to avoid overlapping with the observed data.
descriptionKey:
- Cropland — called "arable land" in the source — is the physical area used to grow crops, including both temporary and permanent crops.
- Projections are based on simulations with FAO's Global Agriculture Perspectives System (GAPS) model, starting from a 2012 base year.
- In the Towards Sustainability scenario, more inclusive societies and more resource-efficient food production systems ensure universal progress towards Sustainable Development Goal targets. Food is mostly produced with environmentally sustainable methods, and greenhouse gas emissions are drastically reduced.

origins.title: The future of food and agriculture - Alternative pathways to 2050
origins.descriptionSnapshot: World totals of arable land, transcribed from Table 4.12 of the report, including a historical value (1970), the base year of the projections (2012), and projections (2030 and 2050) under each of the three scenarios.
origins.description:
FAO's Global Perspectives Studies report "The future of food and agriculture - Alternative pathways to 2050" explores three scenarios of global food and agriculture up to 2050, based on simulations with the FAO Global Agriculture Perspectives System (GAPS) model:
- Business As Usual (BAU): a continuation of historical trends.
- Towards Sustainability (TSS): a shift towards more sustainable food systems.
- Stratified Societies (SSS): a future of increased inequality.
origins.producer: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
origins.citationFull: FAO. 2018. The future of food and agriculture - Alternative pathways to 2050. Rome. 224 pp.
